newsitem.title: USA: Ex-husband of Utah lawmaker faces new charges.
newsitem.headline: Ex-husband of Utah lawmaker faces new charges.

text.p: Federal prosecutors said Wednesday that Joseph Waldholtz, the former husband of Utah Republican Representative Enid Greene, should be jailed immediately for allegedly engaging in a wide range of new criminal conduct.

They said bond for the former Republican political operative should be revoked because he allegedly committed criminal acts including drug use and writing worthless checks since pleading guilty to other charges in June.

"The government alleges that Waldholtz possessed and used heroin, engaged in prescription fraud, stole checks from his stepmother which he then forged with his father's signature and cashed, wrote tens of thousands of dollars of worthless checks and stole credit cards," prosecutors said.
They charged that Waldholtz stole credit cards from his father and a friend and used them for unauthorised purchases.

An FBI investigation turned up the new, alleged illegal activities. A federal judge has ordered Waldholtz to appear for a hearing Thursday on the request by prosecutors that he be jailed right way, pending his sentencing next month on the original criminal charges.
In June, Waldholtz pleaded guilty to four criminal charges including filing false federal reports on contributions to Greene's 1994 campaign for Congress. He was her campaign treasurer.

He pleaded guilty to failing to report campaign contributions, making false statements to the federal election agency, causing his then-wife to file a false tax return in 1993 and bank fraud for a check-kiting scheme.

Under federal sentencing guidelines, the 33-year-old Waldholtz could get 18 to 24 months in prison. At the June hearing, federal judge Norma Holloway Johnson released him on his personal bond, told him to reside with his parents in Squirrell Hill, Pennsylvania, set travel restrictions and ordered him not to commit any new crimes.
Prosecutors charged Waldholtz had violated the judge's order and should be immediately imprisoned. They said the new charges "do not involve in any way Congresswoman Enid Greene."

Greene had been a rising Republican star in Congress until the couple's tangled finances became a major political issue after Waldholtz briefly disappeared late last year. She has maintained that he duped her and got a divorce from him on June 5, the same day that he pleaded guilty.

Greene, who won office as a champion of family values, decided against seeking re-election because of the controversy involving her former husband. Concerning the latest charges, her congressional office referred reporters to her attorney in the case. Lawyers representing Waldholtz had no comment.
